name: 52573-jsonrate-qwen306b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1), driver 570.195.03. The environment seal is configs/env.yaml at `lock: strict`; hold the node exclusively, since the client is CPU-sensitive too.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One engine; no speculative decoding, no LoRA, no KV connector, no offload tier, no router.
architecture: Qwen3ForCausalLM, bf16, 0.6B parameters, ~1.40 GiB of weights in a single safetensors shard; 28 decoder layers, hidden size 1024, 16 query heads over 8 key/value heads of head_dim 128, vocabulary 151936, trained window 40960.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=192, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, 40000 requests bounded, safety_seconds 1800.
workload: HIGH-RATE SHORT STRUCTURED REQUESTS, single turn. guidellm `synthetic_text`, 128 prompt tokens pinned exactly (min = max), and every request carries the same JSON schema in `sampling_params.structured_outputs.json` -- a flat eight-field tagging object, seven closed enumerations and one boolean, `additionalProperties: false`. `output_tokens: 128` is a CEILING and not an achieved length: `ignore_eos` is pinned `false`, so the grammar ends each response as the object closes, on the order of sixty to seventy tokens. Greedy (`temperature: 0.0`), no other sampling parameter moved off its neutral default. `request_format: plain`.
purpose: A content tagging service returning fixed JSON labels for short texts, 192 concurrent streams on one GPU.
launch:
# 52573-jsonrate-qwen306b-1gpu -- the launch config, in `vllm serve --config` form.
# The interpreter and the hardware seal are in configs/env.yaml.

model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
tensor-parallel-size: 1
max-model-len: 512
max-num-seqs: 256

# RUNNER HAZARD: this must stay ONE mapping. vLLM also accepts a separate top-level
# `reasoning-parser` key, and supplying both is a hard failure at engine construction.
structured-outputs-config: {"backend": "xgrammar", "reasoning_parser": "qwen3", "enable_in_reasoning": true}

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# Every prompt is distinct, so nothing can hit; off, every request pays the same prefill. Written
# in negated form because the launcher emits a bare flag for a true value and NOTHING AT ALL for
# a false one, so `enable-prefix-caching: false` would silently leave the engine default (on).
no-enable-prefix-caching: true

# RUNNER HAZARD: leave this disabled. On an SM90 card kernel warmup imports a FlashInfer autotuner
# entry point the pinned `flashinfer-python` does not export, and the engine aborts before serving.
kernel-config: {"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}
